translation_notes: prefixes: BRICK->brick, BSH->bsh, REC->rec, RDF->rdf, OWL->owl, RDFS->rdfs, TAG->tag, SOSA->sosa, SKOS->skos, QUDT->qudt, VCARD->vcard, SH->sh, REF->ref
rdf:type aliases rendered as Turtle `a`: A

9 .add() call sites on the single parameter `graph` (recursively re-passed): one @graph graph at the top of the function body designates it for the whole suite, and every .add() becomes +{ }. The two adjacent, unconditional, same-subject PropertyShape triples (rdf:type + sh:path) were merged into one +{ propshape a sh:PropertyShape ; sh:path prop } (add_run_shared_subject shape); the other 7 stay separate +{ } statements, each guarded by its own if/for exactly as in the original -- no restructuring.

BRICK, BSH, SH etc. stay bound as plain rdflib Namespace objects (from the context shim) alongside the @prefix forms, because the function also uses them as Python values outside any island: `prop.startswith(BRICK)`, `BRICK[prop]`, `BSH[f'...']` slicing off len(BRICK). Only the terms actually written into a triple became prefixed names / interpolations.

Context shim brick_context.py restores: the real IRIs from bricksrc/namespaces.py (package not installed), a plain rdflib.Graph standing in for the heavyweight brickschema.Graph (reached only as define_relationships's *default* graph= value -- irrelevant here since every call passes an explicit graph=), and add_relationships, the sibling top-level function this region calls at its own end (reproduced verbatim from generate_brick.py).

Driver: entry+calls (isomorphism oracle) comparing the graph= kwarg after the call, since the function mutates it in place and returns nothing; the case is a callable building a fresh `definitions` dict per invocation because the region itself consumes it via propdefn.pop(...).
Verified the fixture is not a hollow green: corrupting rdfs:subPropertyOf to rdfs:seeAlso in translated.ldpy flips the check to FAIL (33 vs 33 triples, not isomorphic).

Credit correction (2026-11-02, corpus/403 defect 3): dropped `@prefix` for `rec:`, `owl:`, `tag:`, `sosa:`, `skos:`, `qudt:`, `vcard:`, `ref:`, declared by the mechanical draft but never used as a term in the translated region (and not among the bindings the original sets on its graph); `rdfeval check` stays OK.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the prop_types and domains loops become `graph += [...]` comprehensions; the two PropertyShape triples become one `graph += [...]`; `"range" in propdefn.keys()` + `pop` becomes `propdefn.pop("range", None)` (absent and None take the same no-op path, and propshape is still read only when a range is given, so the stale or unbound propshape of a non-Brick property behaves as before); `.keys()` goes from the two other membership tests; the datatype if/else becomes one add with `SH["or"] if dtype_defn == BSH.NumericValue else SH.datatype` as predicate (the equality holds only for that very URIRef, so the object is the same term); expected_properties and other_properties fold into one dict comprehension over propdefn.items(). Kept: `len(definitions) == 0` (it raises on None where `not definitions` would return), both asserts, the order of the writes around the recursive call, and the two separate `prop.startswith(BRICK)` tests (the recursion sits between them).

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `+{ }` everywhere, loops with `+{ }` where Python has comprehensions, `propshape = bsh:{f"...Shape"}` (the local part is always a str, so it equals BSH[...]), the datatype ternary inside the predicate interpolation with prefixed names. `BRICK[prop]` stays Python: `brick:{prop}` concatenates str(prop) and raises on None, where Namespace.__getitem__ yields the bare namespace for a non-str key; the Collection call stays Python.
